newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Fernandez sees no need to devalue.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Fernandez sees no need to devalue.

text.p: Argentine Economy Minister Roque Fernandez predicted Friday there would be no need to devalue the peso, now pegged to the dollar at par, during his term.
"I want you to rest assured that I will not need to devalue during my term," Fernandez said in a speech to financial executives.
He also forecast the nation's exports would increase 7.0 percent this year to a record $22.5 billion.
"This (the export outlook) demonstrates that the old concept under which it was necessary to devalue to make our exports competitive was mistaken," Fernandez said.

Asked by an executive whether the minister had plans to end peso-dollar parity introduced in 1991, Fernandez said, "Changing the exchange rate would introduce a level of uncertainty that would be negative for the economy."
He reiterated government forecasts that the economy will grow by 3.0 percent this year and 5.0 percent in 1997. GDP fell 4.6 percent last year.
